keyFindings: Cushioning: Firm-leaning but protective ride; 42/32 mm stack and ZoomX-over-ReactX feel plush/protective with little ground feel, though the heel feels clunky/slappy from a sharp rocker while midfoot/forefoot transitions are smoother.
Responsiveness: Energy return is moderate at best; ZoomX adds a little bounce/premium feel, but the shoe is not very springy or snappy, and pace changes feel limited by weight and firm tuning.

Stability: Strong guidance through rearfoot and midfoot from tall sidewalls, sole flaring, and a structured chassis; heel counter is very stiff, and medial/lateral support is prominent throughout transitions.
Durability: Outsole and materials tested very well so far (reported no outsole denting at ~40 miles), midsole has held its character without softening, and traction is strong on dry/wet roads.

Cushioning: Max-cushioned 42 mm heel / 32 mm forefoot platform with ZoomX core + ReactX carrier feels deep, plush, soft, and protective, with smooth transitions, soft yet stable heel landings, and a decently flexible forefoot toe-off.

Responsiveness: ZoomX gives a reactive, springy ride with mild bounce and a lighter-on-foot feel than the weight suggests, but reviewers noted it is not especially energetic/snappy and can feel clunky at faster paces.

Stability: Guidance is subtle rather than rigid, coming from high medial/lateral sidewalls and the midfoot support system; a substantial near-rigid heel counter, rigid lateral heel overlay, and strong heel/midfoot lockdown provide secure lateral and rearfoot support.
Durability: This excerpt does not report clear outsole wear testing or long-term material breakdown, so durability conclusions are limited from the provided text.

Cushioning: Very plush and soft underfoot from the high-stack ZoomX + ReactX setup (42 mm heel/32 mm forefoot), with strong comfort and impact protection; forefoot/toe-off can feel dull and overly soft on longer runs.
Responsiveness: ZoomX adds some energy return so it does not feel dead, but overall ride is low-geared with limited bounce/snappiness and less bite at toe-off.

Stability: Surprisingly stable for a max-cushion shoe due to a wide planted platform, solid arch/midfoot support, slight medial rise, and supportive upper overlays; heel counter is intentionally not overly rigid.
Durability: No meaningful long-term outsole wear or upper longevity data was provided in the review; only traction/grip was noted as surprisingly good.
